title: Cheat Sheet: Compute Engine vs GKE vs Cloud Run vs Functions — D4
purpose: Shows identities, trust boundaries, policy checks, and audit evidence.
routing_rationale: Mastering Google Cloud compute selection requires evaluating three core dimensions: abstraction level (IaaS vs CaaS vs FaaS), scaling characteristics (scale-to-zero vs pre-warmed), and protocol support (HTTP vs raw TCP/UDP).

nodes.label: Stateless HTTP / gRPC Container?
nodes.detail: Standard microservices responding to web and mobile API requests.

nodes.label: Custom OS / Raw TCP / Bare Metal?
nodes.detail: Legacy Windows, kernel modules, high-performance computing, or game servers.

nodes.label: Cloud Run (First Choice)
nodes.detail: Fastest time-to-market; scales from 0 to 1,000 instances; zero cluster maintenance.

nodes.label: Cloud Functions (2nd Gen)
nodes.detail: Lightweight event handlers triggered by Cloud Storage uploads or Pub/Sub events.

nodes.label: GKE Autopilot
nodes.detail: Complex multi-container pods, stateful workloads, service mesh, and custom networking.

nodes.label: Compute Engine MIGs
nodes.detail: Full root access, custom kernel extensions, Windows Server, and local NVMe SSDs.

steps.title: Serverless-First Evaluation
steps.action: Google recommends Cloud Run as default compute for all containerized HTTP services.
steps.why_traversal: Delivers highest developer velocity and lowest total cost of ownership.

steps.title: Orchestration & Infrastructure Path
steps.action: Non-HTTP, multi-container, or stateful systems route to GKE Autopilot or Compute Engine.
steps.why_traversal: Provides granular infrastructure control when serverless constraints are breached.

scenarios.label: Selected Compute Engine for Idle Microservice
scenarios.root_cause: Deployed low-traffic internal webhook on 3 always-on Compute Engine VMs.
scenarios.diverted_path: Cost $220/month for 15 requests/day; Cloud Run would have cost $0.00/month.
scenarios.recovery: Migrate stateless idle microservices to Cloud Run scale-to-zero.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.

scenarios.label: Dependency unavailable
scenarios.root_cause: A required API or downstream dependency is unavailable.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.
